explanation: Build the distinct set of values. A smaller distinct count means at least one value appeared twice.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n values. Each of the n values is inserted or tested once with expected constant-time hashing.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. At most n distinct values are retained in the set.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A set contains one entry for each distinct input value. Its size equals the input length exactly when every occurrence has a different value. A smaller size therefore proves a repeated value, and every repeat makes the size smaller.
walkthrough: For [8,1,5,8], the distinct set is {8,1,5}, with size 3 instead of 4. The second 8 introduces no new set entry, so return true.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton arrays contain no duplicate.
A repeat need not be adjacent.
Negative values are ordinary set keys.
